title: Low-degree cohomology of a right derived functor sees only low degrees
statement: Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with right derived functor $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ computed by K-injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Let $n\in\mathbf Z$ and let $c:L\to M$ be a morphism of $D^+(\mathcal A)$ such that $\mathcal H^i(c):\mathcal H^i(L)\to\mathcal H^i(M)$ is an isomorphism for every $i\leq n$ and a monomorphism for $i=n+1$. Then $\mathcal H^j(Rv(c)):\mathcal H^j(RvL)\to\mathcal H^j(RvM)$ is an isomorphism for every $j\leq n$. In particular, for $K\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and the canonical truncation $c_n:\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$, the map $\mathcal H^n(Rv\,\tau_{\leq n}K)\to\mathcal H^n(RvK)$ induced by $c_n$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing, line 5497), part (2) and its proof (lines 5525-5541): the triangle $\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to\tau_{\geq a+1}K\to$, part (1) applied to its third vertex, and the long exact cohomology sequence; the statement above is that proof with the cone of $c$ in place of $\tau_{\geq n+1}K$
